headline: Frontier AI Takes Korea's Toughest Exam
summary: Three leading AI models tackled Korea's notoriously rigorous Suneung entrance exam and missed only three questions. The failures expose critical reasoning and cultural blindspots in modern LLMs.

slides.title: Frontier AI Meets the Suneung Test
slides.subtitle: Three top frontier models tackled Korea's brutal college entrance exam.
slides.body: Korea's Suneung is famous for fiendishly difficult logic puzzles. Top models nearly aced it, but stumbled on three revealing edge cases.
slides.deep_dive: Standard AI benchmarks are hitting performance ceilings. Real-world standardized exams provide an unvarnished stress test for genuine deductive reasoning.
slides.key_fact: Frontier models missed only three questions across the entire high-stakes evaluation.
slides.why_it_matters: Proves frontier models excel at standard logic, but edge-case reasoning traps still break synthetic comprehension.

slides.title: Beyond Saturated Western Benchmarks
slides.subtitle: Why existing AI evaluation suites no longer tell the full story.
slides.body: Traditional benchmarks suffer from test-set contamination and English bias. Highly guarded national exams offer tamper-proof benchmarks for true general intelligence.
slides.deep_dive: The Suneung features novel questions locked under state security until test day, preventing test contamination in LLM pre-training corpora.
slides.key_fact: Uncontaminated, freshly printed national exams eliminate training data memorization.
slides.why_it_matters: Engineering teams need fresh, non-contaminated evaluation sets to measure real model reasoning.

slides.title: Where Model Reasoning Breaks Down
slides.subtitle: Tracing how complex multi-step questions tripped up the models.
slides.body: The missed questions exposed a specific breakdown in high-order deduction when visual and linguistic traps intersect.

steps.title: Linguistic Ambiguity
steps.desc: Subtle linguistic cues in Korean lost precision during internal token representation.

steps.title: Diagram-Text Fusion
steps.desc: Models struggled to correlate dense geometric constraints with nuanced textual prompts.

steps.title: Distractor Traps
steps.desc: Deliberately designed human elimination traps lured models toward plausible-sounding fallacies.

slides.title: Standard Evals vs Extreme Exams
slides.subtitle: How the Suneung differs from conventional academic benchmarks.
slides.body: Extreme national exams test capabilities that common synthetic benchmarks completely overlook.

slides.title: Building Production-Grade Reasoning
slides.subtitle: Lessons for AI engineers designing mission-critical pipelines.
slides.body: Models can score in the top percentile while still failing basic cultural nuance or diagrammatic constraints in production.
slides.deep_dive: If your application relies on high-stakes enterprise logic, synthetic evals are insufficient. You must curate adversarial, out-of-distribution reasoning benchmarks.
slides.key_fact: High general test scores do not guarantee zero failure on adversarial edge cases.
slides.why_it_matters: Teams must implement multi-agent verification layers when processing culturally dense or multimodal data.

slides.title: The Next Frontier of Model Evaluation
slides.subtitle: Three key lessons from testing frontier AI on the Suneung.
slides.body: The race is shifting from memorized pattern matching to adversarial, cross-lingual logical deduction.
takeaways: Uncontaminated real-world exams reveal blindspots that synthetic benchmarks hide.
Multimodal fusion and deceptive distractor filtering remain active frontier challenges.
Cross-lingual nuance requires deep semantic grounding, not simple token translation.
